posts.title: Head Bobbing Motion
posts.author: Jeah Kim
posts.authorRole: Interactive XR designer and biomedical communicator.
content: While many motion-tracking accessories exist today, the goal here was to track footsteps while user walk in place using only the VR headset. To get there, I referred to a study that evaluated a VR bobbing mechanism where participants adjusted oscillation amplitudes for comfort. The findings showed a strong preference for vertical oscillation, with consistent amplitudes across speeds (±0.695 cm for walking and ±1.351 cm for running), while lateral roll varied more (±0.186° for walking and ±0.334° for running).
Building on this, I focused on two key factors for replicating natural walking:
2. Lateral rotation—the subtle rolling motion of the head
